kind: constructed synthetic portfolios with fixture-author expectations; no human labels
method: Executed: the prototype functions in apps/desktop/test/outcome-gap-research run on the portfolios in fixtures.ts. Expected verdicts, reasons and suggestion sets were declared by the fixture author from the written rules before the code was run.
Executed: invariances (what must not change when outcomes, scores or assessments change) and a dismissal check.
Executed, constructed: four simpler rules scored on the same fixture (baselines).
Source reading: the manual-review side of the desk comparison.
Real-contract lane (added by evaluation.test.ts): synthetic data written through the app’s real writers into a migrated database and read back by the read-only adapter.
Review gates are author-declared and not statistically derived (GATES in contract.ts). No inference is made about any real person.

portfolios.title: Enough data, if follow-ups A and B existed

portfolios.title: Syndicated copies dominate
portfolios.what: 22 mature sends, each seen as 4 copies (88 rows read for 22 requisitions).

portfolios.title: Most outcomes are unknown
portfolios.what: 24 mature sends, 20 with no recorded outcome.

portfolios.title: Identity is mostly the weak tier
portfolios.what: 22 mature sends keyed only by company/title/location text.

portfolios.title: Titles say Kubernetes, nothing was assessed
portfolios.what: 12 jobs with a high score and a Kubernetes-flavoured title, no assessment: there is no requirement evidence, so there must be no requirement row and no suggestion.

portfolios.title: Assessments made against three different CV versions
portfolios.what: 12 current assessments over CV hashes 5/4/3: the evidence classes are not comparable across CV versions.

portfolios.title: Assessments summarised under another rule version or an unknown one

portfolios.title: Kubernetes / K8s: merged only by the person
portfolios.what: 10 current assessments; "Kubernetes" in 2, "K8s" in 2, "Kube" in 1. Without a person-confirmed alias no wording reaches the recurrence threshold of 3; the person confirming that they are one thing makes it 5.

portfolios.title: Two roles at one employer and a reapplication
portfolios.what: 3 requisitions at the same employer; one was applied for twice. Each role keeps its own requirement lane and outcome.

outcomesFlipped.claim: Making every sent application rejected, or every one an interview, changes no requirement row, no lane count, no eligibility row and no suggestion; only the labelled outcome context moves.

scoresChanged.claim: Setting every fit score to missing, to 0, or to 99 changes no requirement row and no suggestion. A score of 0 is a recorded score and is counted as scored; missing is counted as unscored.

actual.note: An evaluator opinion about fit. It is not a requirement, a gap or an outcome, and it is not used to compute any row here.

allMissing.note: An evaluator opinion about fit. It is not a requirement, a gap or an outcome, and it is not used to compute any row here.

allZero.note: An evaluator opinion about fit. It is not a requirement, a gap or an outcome, and it is not used to compute any row here.

noAssessmentMeansNoRequirements.claim: Removing every assessment leaves the same job titles, scores and outcomes but no requirement row and no requirement suggestion; nothing is inferred from the rest.

dismissal.claim: A dismissed suggestion leaves the visible list, stays inspectable, does not return when more supporting jobs arrive (it reports how many newer ones), and dismissing changes no suggestion and no input.

baselines.note: Constructed comparisons on the rich_projected portfolio only. Each is a simpler rule someone might write; none is shipped behaviour.

method: Fixture: the rich_projected portfolio (30 requisitions) with invented free text on some jobs (Fit check, next step, notes).
MANUAL side = SOURCE READING of what the current screens show (file citations below). Nothing was executed on the manual side and no person was observed.
PROTOTYPE side = EXECUTED: the views run on the same fixture.
Unit = counted operations (one job record opened = 1). It is not time, effort, accuracy or a usability result. No human labels were collected; the "better" column is the fixture author’s reading.
The rich portfolio is projected data. Where the answer needs a field production does not record, the row says so and the comparison is of design capability, not of what the app does today.

surfaces.fitCheck: apps/desktop/src/components/saved/SavedJobDrawer.tsx ("Fit check": job.gapAnalysis, free text, saved by the person)
surfaces.brief: apps/desktop/src/components/brief/ApplicationBriefPanel.tsx (strengths / gaps / open questions, capped at BRIEF_LIST_CAP = 5 per list; eligibility; "Where this came from")
surfaces.found: apps/desktop/src/components/search/VacancyDetail.tsx ("Found with": queries, shown only for a lead in the latest scan report)

manual.opensWhat: each saved job’s drawer: the brief’s strengths/gaps/open-questions lists plus any kept Fit check
manual.aggregationDone: by the person, by hand: nothing counts across jobs

prototype.blindSpot: 2 job(s) have the finding only as kept free text ("Terraform"), which the structured view cannot read; they are reported as not assessed, not guessed.

questions.question: Is a recurring missing item a gap I recorded, or just something my CV does not show?

manual.perJobDistinctionExists: yes: the brief lists "gaps" and "open questions" separately for an assessed job

questions.betterForPerJobDetail: tie (both separate the two for one job)

questions.question: Do the jobs I chose repeatedly conflict with something I said I need?
Which source or search variant do my sent applications come from, and what happened to them?

manual.opensWhat: each sent application’s row (status) and its saved-job drawer (“Where this came from”)
manual.sourceReadable: yes per job (brief: provider and link of each copy)
manual.queryVariantReadable: no for a saved job: "Found with" appears only on a lead in the latest scan report and the variant is not stored with the saved job (proved in workspace-contract.test.ts)
manual.outcomeReadable: status only: no date, source or reason

requiresProjectedFields: query attribution carried into the brief (follow-up B)
prototype.onTodaysData: no_go: query variant not recorded, too few mature sends (see the real-contract lane)

questions.betterForCountingAcrossJobs: prototype, only if the projected fields exist; on today’s data neither side can name the variant
questions.betterForPerJobDetail: manual for source; neither for variant

questions.question: What did a recruiter or contact say that bears on my search?

manual.opensWhat: the application’s next step (table) and notes (drawer)

prototype.answer: none: notes and next-step text are deliberately not read, parsed or aggregated
prototype.blindSpot: 3 job(s) hold context only in free text

questions.betterForCountingAcrossJobs: manual (the prototype cannot see it by design)

totals.note: Counted record opens, not time. The prototype also needs the underlying data to exist; on today’s data q4 is a no-go and q1–q3 depend on how many jobs the person assessed.

limits: No human did any of this; the manual side is a reading of the source, the prototype side is a run on constructed data.
A person with 3 saved jobs does not need an aggregate: the counted advantage only appears as the number of jobs grows.
Free text can carry the decisive fact. The prototype ignores it on purpose, so it is complementary to manual review, not a replacement.
No claim is made about decision quality, time saved, hiring outcomes or user preference.

unknowns: No human labels: every expected value was written by the implementer. Nothing here is human validated.
No real job search was used. The portfolios say nothing about how often these patterns occur for a real person, employer or ATS.
Nothing is known about whether any suggestion would be useful, understood or acted on; no usability study was run.
The rich portfolio relies on fields production does not record (query attribution, status events, exposure counts); its go_review verdicts describe the contract, not the app.
The review gates (counts and shares) are author-declared. They were not tuned or validated on data and could be wrong in either direction.
Maturity (28 days) has no empirical basis; employers answer on very different time scales and many never answer.
Exact-text recurrence under-counts spelling variants; person-confirmed aliases fix that only for wordings the person notices.
No provider, token, latency or cost telemetry was collected or is claimed: nothing in the prototype calls a model.
limits: Selected jobs are survivorship-filtered: deleted saved jobs are gone.
Correlation between a requirement and an outcome is never presented as cause; outcomes are context only.
A requirement a CV cannot evidence is not a missing skill.
The conclusion is about whether automated calibration is supportable (it is not), not about hiring outcomes.

unrecoverable.detail: No workspace table or brief column stores which query variant produced a saved job (LeadQueryProvenance exists only in the scan report JSON).
Leads shown, skipped or ignored are not stored; only jobs the person saved or applied to exist.
applications.status is one mutable value with no change time, source or reason; the only application date is applied_at.
Deleting a saved job removes its row (and an unreferenced brief): jobs the person dropped are invisible, so "selected" is survivorship-filtered.
cv_documents keeps no version history; a CV or JD version is only a hash, so compatibility is hash equality, not a diff.
